{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "He did not turn when she stepped onto the platform, though the stone rang faintly under her boots and she knew he heard it. The bellows-sound had stopped. In its absence the silence was so complete she could hear the chart shift under his fingers as he smoothed the torn corner flat.

"You took the long way," he said.

"There was only one way."

"There is always only one way. That is what makes it long." He turned the chair then, slowly, its iron feet scraping a circle into the dust, and she saw his face and found that it had not aged, or had aged in some direction she did not have a word for. The eyes were the same. Everything else had been rearranged around them.

She looked at the ring set into the center of the platform. It was large enough to moor a ship, and there was no ship, and no water near enough to float one. "What is that for?"

"For whatever comes to be tied to it." He folded the chart once, twice, and held it out to her. "You will want this back. I finished the part you couldn't."

She did not take it. Her hands were still white with salt, and she understood, dimly, that if she touched the paper the causeway behind her would be gone, that she would have chosen. The light on its post had been a point. Now, when she let herself look, it was nothing at all.

"How long have you been here?"

"Since before you left," he said. "That was the arrangement. You just weren't told your half of it.""}
